title: How much of a gold dinar is a cowrie shell?
description: Four old coins are linked in a chain, a dinar, a dramma, a pana and a cowrie shell. Each coin is a fraction of the one before it, so one pana and then one cowrie shell are found as parts of a dinar by multiplying the fractions along the chain. Keeko thinks a pana is one quarter of a dinar.
teaching_notes: One idea: when each coin is a fraction of the one before it, the value of a small coin in the largest coin is the product of the fractions along the chain. Watch for students who stop after the first link and call a pana a quarter of a dinar.

source: Take 1 gold dinar = 12 silver drammas, 1 dramma = 4 copper panas and 1 pana = 30 cowrie shells. How much of a gold dinar is 1 copper pana, and how much is 1 cowrie shell?
video_script.why: A learner sees that a coin in a chain is a part of a part, and its value in the largest coin is the product of the fractions along the chain.
video_script.substitution: the book's own coins, with the gold dinar, the silver dramma, the copper pana and the cowrie shell
video_script.anchor: a chain of four coins, a gold dinar, a silver dramma, a copper pana and a cowrie shell, each smaller than the one before
video_script.wrong_move: stops at the first link, one pana is one quarter of a dramma, and calls it a part of a dinar
video_script.payoff_line: One cowrie shell is one one thousand four hundred fortieth of a dinar.

final_answer.spoken: one pana is one forty eighth of a dinar, and one cowrie shell is one one thousand four hundred fortieth of a dinar

video_script.fraction_reading: one twelfth, one quarter, one forty eighth, one thirtieth, one one thousand four hundred fortieth
maths_rules: 1 pana = 30 cowrie shells, so 1 cowrie shell = 1/30 pana
1 cowrie shell = 1/30 of 1/48 dinar = 1/30 x 1/48 = (1 x 1)/(30 x 48) = 1/1440 dinar
the slip: 1/4 is a part of a dramma, not of a dinar
video_script.design: The four coins in a row, each linked to the next by an arrow carrying its fraction; the working band multiplies the fractions along the arrows.

<bookmark mark='gold'/>One gold dinar is worth twelve silver drammas.
One silver dramma is worth four copper panas.
<bookmark mark='copper'/>One copper pana is worth thirty cowrie shells.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How much of a gold dinar is one copper pana, and how much is one cowrie shell?

<bookmark mark='pana'/>One dramma is four panas, so one pana is one quarter of a dramma.

<bookmark mark='mult'/>One twelfth times one quarter is one over twelve times four.
<bookmark mark='frac'/>One pana is one forty eighth of a dinar.

<bookmark mark='of'/>Take one thirtieth of one forty eighth of a dinar.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>One thirtieth times one forty eighth is one over thirty times forty eight.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks one quarter of a dinar is one pana.
A pana is a quarter of a dramma, after all.
<bookmark mark='dram'/>But a dramma is only one twelfth of a dinar.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The twelve must be used too, and the two fractions are multiplied.
